look_here_first: START WITH THE TOP FACE (ADAXIAL SURFACE) OF A MATURE LEAF OR SHOWY WHITE-MARGINED BRACT: snow-on-the-prairie is conspicuously HAIRY ABOVE. Then inspect the LONG NARROW linear-to-narrowly oblanceolate bracts. Snow-on-the-mountain (E. marginata) generally has smooth/glabrous upper leaf and bract faces with broader elliptic/obovate bracts. BOTH species can be very white: amount, patchiness or continuity of white are NOT dependable diagnostic differences. Check these TWO independent characters together. Upper bracts are modified leaves, not petals; the actual flower-like inflorescence is a tiny cyathium; developing fruit is a three-lobed capsule. Hays-area learner admission remains RANGE_UNRESOLVED and excluded from native metrics even though the taxon is native to Texas at a state scale.

key_traits.label: Family pattern
key_traits.text: Euphorbia: milky latex; true flowers are highly reduced and grouped in a cyathium; the showy white structures here are bracts and gland appendages, not ordinary petals.

key_traits.label: Growth form
key_traits.text: Annual, taprooted, erect to suberect herb, commonly about 40–110 cm tall.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Cauline leaves narrowly obovate/elliptic to lanceolate; uppermost leaves and bracts develop conspicuous white margins.

key_traits.label: Pubescence
key_traits.text: Stems, leaves, bracts, inflorescence, and capsules are conspicuously pilose/villous; hairs may be several millimeters long.

key_traits.label: Bracts
key_traits.text: Largest showy bracts are long and narrow, typically linear to narrowly oblanceolate rather than broadly elliptic.

key_traits.label: Cyathium
key_traits.text: Small flower-like cyathia with usually 4–5 nectar glands bearing white petal-like appendages.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: TEXAS native at state scale but Hays project native-range threshold still on HOLD; do not count as target-certified.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Annual erect/taprooted herb, often about 40–100 cm, occasionally branching; habitat/habit not species proof.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Ordinary stem leaves alternate; very narrow white-margined terminal bracts often linear or narrowly oblanceolate.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Upper (adaxial) leaf and bract surfaces have conspicuous soft hairs; key character versus *E. marginata*, which is usually glabrous on those surfaces.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Tiny true reduced flowers occur inside cyathia; rounded white gland appendages can look deceptively like petals.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Fruit a three-lobed capsule, densely soft-hairy; fruit hairiness alone will NOT distinguish *E. marginata*.

lookalikes.differences: Against E. marginata, prioritize two characters together: upper-surface hairiness and bract width. E. bicolor is the narrow-and-hairy plant; E. marginata is generally the broader-and-glabrous-above plant.
